Welcome to the actual tutorial for my bioinf576 project. The only thing left is to run MEME on the last I Here are the Following files that were run on the preprocessing-pipelines 1. Tet2_wildtype_RNAseq_rep1, SRR21586232 2. Tet2_wildtype_RNAseq_rep2, SRR21586231 3. Tet2_knockout_RNAseq_rep1, SRR21586226 4. Tet2_knockout_RNAseq_rep2, SRR21586226

  1. Tet2_wildtype_CUT&TAG_rep1, SRR21586222
  2. Tet2_knockout_CUT&TAG_rep1, SRR21586221

SnakeMake Pre-Processing Commands

UNIX commands (Ran on the Umich Great Lakes Cluster)

Before running Ensure your directory tree looks similar to the example below

snakemake/ |── Snakefile # Main workflow |── config/ │ └── config.yaml # Parameters, sample info, etc. |─ envs/ │ └── chip_pipeline.yaml # Conda environments |── scripts/ │ ├── custom_analysis.R # R analysis scripts │ └── helper_functions.py # Python helpers |── data/ │ └── chip_data/ | # Raw fastq files, e.g., SRRxxxx_1.fastq |── chip_pipleine/ └── SnakeFile/ #SnakeFile to be called

Repeat this structure for RNA-Seq Pre-Processing Pipeline

You should alread have conda installed, else: https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/stable/user-guide/install/linux.html Install SnakeMake if you have not already # Linux wget https://repo.anaconda.com/miniconda/Miniconda3-latest-Linux-x86_64.sh bash Miniconda3-latest-Linux-x86_64.sh

macOS

wget https://repo.anaconda.com/miniconda/Miniconda3-latest-MacOSX-x86_64.sh bash Miniconda3-latest-MacOSX-x86_64.sh

Creat a Cona Env conda create -n snakemake-env -c conda-forge -c bioconda snakemake conda activate snakemake-env

Make your environments conda config –set channel_priority strict or that does not work channel_priority flexible

cd to the env folder conda env create –name rna_pipeline –file rna_pipeline.yaml conda env create –name chip_pipeline –file chip_pipeline.yaml

Make Sure you have the paired-end Sequences (ChIP/CUT&TAG, RNA-seq) into their seperate folders under ./data/chip_data, and ./data/rna_data

conda activate one of the environments

conda activate rna_pipeline or conda activate rna_pipeline ### SnakeMake Commands

cd to the respective pre-processing folder

run using snakemake –dry-run to check the pipeline is working

snakemake –cores 32 # for the real datasets

As of 4/11/2025 we must use some other datasets until the real ones are ready

We are using a real dataset but not the one are planning.

I then had to create a count matrix for DeSeq2

RNA-Seq Analysis

need to reformat the rnaseqdat grab the merged counts tsv

tet2_wt_rp1 <- read_tsv("./SRR21586232 RNAseq WT/merged_counts_tet2wt_rep1.txt", comment = "#")

Reformating function for post process

colnames(tet2_wt_rp1)[7] = "WT_rep1"
colnames(tet2_wt_rp2)[7] = "WT_rep2"
colnames(tet2_ko_rp1)[7] = "KO_rep1"
colnames(tet2_ko_rp2)[7] = "KO_rep2"
WT_KO_rep1 <- left_join(tet2_wt_rp1, tet2_wt_rp2, by = "Geneid")
WT_KO_rep2 <- left_join(tet2_ko_rp1, tet2_ko_rp2, by = "Geneid")
tet2_RNASeq <- left_join(WT_KO_rep1, WT_KO_rep2, by = "Geneid") %>% 
  dplyr::select("Geneid", "WT_rep1", "WT_rep2", "KO_rep1", "KO_rep2")
tet2_RNASeq
## # A tibble: 49,997 × 5
##    Geneid WT_rep1 WT_rep2 KO_rep1 KO_rep2
##    <chr>    <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>
##  1 TrnP       463     485     338     247
##  2 TrnT         3      11       7       3
##  3 CYTB     47180   46485   55295   40037
##  4 TrnE         7      15       8      12
##  5 ND6      13740   17217   11029    9665
##  6 ND5      47490   50701   43956   31347
##  7 TrnL2      176     169      89      98
##  8 TrnS2      200     200     110      81
##  9 TrnH       303     297     184     156
## 10 ND4      21480   20958   20514   15908
## # ℹ 49,987 more rows
countData <- as.matrix(tet2_RNASeq[ , -1])
rownames(countData) <- tet2_RNASeq[[1]]
colData <- data.frame(
  row.names = colnames(countData),
  condition = c("WT", "WT", "KO", "KO")
)
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = countData,
  colData = colData,
  design = ~ condition
)
## converting counts to integer mode
## Warning in DESeqDataSet(se, design = design, ignoreRank): some variables in
## design formula are characters, converting to factors
dds <- DESeq(dds)
## estimating size factors
## estimating dispersions
## gene-wise dispersion estimates
## mean-dispersion relationship
## final dispersion estimates
## fitting model and testing
normalized_counts <- counts(dds, normalized = TRUE)

results_table <- results(dds)

results_frame <- as.data.frame(results_table)
Tet2_WTvKO <- tibble::rownames_to_column(results_frame, "GeneID")

#this function needs to be generalized. How? Need to take a page out of the clusterprofiler
mmu_entrezid_to_genename <- function(entrez_vector) {
  #requires both of these packages to run
  #require("biomaRt")
  #require("org.Mmu.eg.db")
  #connect to the Ensembl database for Mmu
  ensembl = useMart("ensembl", dataset = "mmusculus_gene_ensembl")
  #getting the corresponding Entrez Gene IDs
  entrezid_genename_df <- getBM(attributes = c("external_gene_name", "entrezgene_id"), filters = "external_gene_name", values = entrez_vector, mart = ensembl)
  #return both the df and the vector
  return(entrezid_genename_df)
}
entrez_ids <- mmu_entrezid_to_genename(Tet2_RNAChIP_unique$GeneID)
entrez_ids
